adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Calendar.createEvent` to accept a `credentialId` and updates GoogleCalendarService to select the destination calendar matching that `credentialId` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), but non-Google implementations do not use the new parameter and instead always take the first destination calendar. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` derives `eventsUrl` from `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`, i.e., only the first entry. In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent`/`createAttendees`/`updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` similarly use only the first destination calendar’s `externalId`. In `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (CalDav/base), calendar selection is filtered using only the first destination calendar’s `externalId`. Meanwhile, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` for collective events and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, but `CalendarManager.createEvent` ignores the passed `externalId` and always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. Net effect: for multiple destination calendars, non-Google services will create/update/delete using the main host destination calendar rather than the member’s matching destination calendar, which can write to the wrong calendar or fail.
